entities.summary:
Ubaldo of Gallura (ubaldo-of-gallura) was a medieval Judge of Gallura, son of Lamberto di Eldizio and Elena de Lacon, who ruled from 1225 to 1238. He was the head of the giudicato of Gallura and held sway over parts of the Sardinian islands, including the coastal towns of Castelsardo, Alghero, and Terrazzas. His tenure saw the rise of the Visconti family's influence in the region.


    As a member of the Sardinian nobility, Ubaldo played a key role in the island's complex web of alliances and rivalries during the 13th century. His leadership during this period had a lasting impact on the political landscape of Sardinia, shaping the course of the giudicato's history and influencing the future of the island's ruling families.


    Despite the limited scope of his domain, Ubaldo's legacy extended beyond the borders of Gallura, reflecting the intricate connections between the Sardinian giudicati and the broader Mediterranean world.


    One of the most striking aspects of Ubaldo's rule was the cultural and economic exchange that took place during his tenure, as Gallura became a hub for the trade of goods such as wool, textiles, and wine.
